findings.mechanism: The code sets model.similarity_fn_name = "cosine" as a side effect, which is an in-place mutation of the caller's model. This can alter the model's behavior in unexpected ways if the model is reused with a different loss or if the model's similarity function is used elsewhere. The parent CoSENTLoss does not read this attribute, so the numerical result of the loss is not affected, but the side effect is a defect.
findings.trigger: Creating an instance of SparseCoSENTLoss with any SparseEncoder model.
findings.consequence: The model's similarity_fn_name is permanently changed to "cosine" after the loss object is created, which could cause incorrect behavior in other loss functions or when the model is reused.
